cards.back: The **art and science of planning and leading software projects** — a sub-discipline of project management where software projects are planned, implemented, monitored and controlled.

cards.front: The 3 roles of a project manager
cards.back: **Leader** (direction, vision, builds the team), **Liaison** (communication bridge between clients/team/management), **Mentor** (guidance, cohesion, growth).
Balance **Scope · Time · Cost**, with **Quality at the centre**. No corner changes without trade-offs in the other two.
**Initiation → Planning → Execution → Monitoring & Control → Closure.** This management lifecycle *wraps* the engineering SDLC.
**Release planning** (several months, features) and **Iteration planning** (2–4 weeks, the next increment in detail).
**Effort points completed per iteration.** Used to forecast total effort and choose how many stories fit an iteration.
**Fixed time, variable scope** — ship an increment every iteration; if features don't fit, **reduce scope, never extend the schedule**. Dev tasks = **4–16 h**; developers **volunteer** for them.
Hierarchical decomposition of a project into manageable work packages. Principles: **100% rule** (full coverage), **mutually exclusive** components, appropriate level.
**E = a·(KLOC)^b** person-months · **T = c·(E)^d** months · **Persons = E/T**. Organic (2.4, 1.05, 2.5, 0.38), semi-detached (3.0, 1.12, 2.5, 0.35), embedded (3.6, 1.20, 2.5, 0.32).
**Organic** (small/familiar), **Semi-detached** (medium), **Embedded** (complex/tight). Three models by accuracy: **Basic → Intermediate → Detailed**.
**Function points** size by functionality (inputs, outputs, inquiries, files, interfaces) → **language-independent**, derivable early. **LOC** is language-dependent and late.
Activities (vertical) vs **time scale** (horizontal): duration bars, dependencies, progress, milestones. Shows **what is done and when**.
The **longest path** of dependent activities, with **zero slack**, setting the **minimum project duration**. To finish earlier, shorten the *critical* path.
Compartmentalization · Interdependency · Time allocation · Effort validation · Defined responsibilities · Defined outcomes · Defined milestones.
**Project** (schedule/resources), **Product** (software quality/performance), **Business** (the organisation). A risk can be both project & product.
**Identification → Analysis → Planning → Monitoring.** **Risk Exposure = Probability × Impact** (used to prioritise).
**Avoidance** (remove source), **Mitigation** (reduce probability/impact), **Transfer** (insurance/contract), **Acceptance** (contingency plan).
**R**esponsible (the doer, many allowed), **A**ccountable (**only ONE**, the buck stops here), **C**onsulted (two-way, before), **I**nformed (one-way, after).
Project Plan · WBS · Schedule · Resource Management Plan · Communication Plan · Risk Management Plan · Role Definitions (RACI).
Shared **quality standards** (peer accountability), **knowledge sharing**, **continuity** (survives departures), **continuous-improvement** culture.
Multiple **views** of one system, each for a stakeholder/purpose, hiding irrelevant detail — like Bengaluru mapped by wards, electricity (BESCOM), water (BWSSB), pincodes, assembly.

Failures: tight coupling (shared global memory), race conditions, unreviewed legacy reuse, no fault isolation, no logging. Lessons: **separation of concerns, fail-safe design, defensive programming, redundancy**.

**Architecture** = system-level (scaling, subsystem comms, system-wide security, deployment). **Design** = component-level (a feature's algorithms, data structures, UI). The **Zipper model** blends up-front + iterative.
**Pipes & filters:** data flows through independent filters (no shared state, acyclic) — e.g. a **compiler**. **Layered:** adjacent layers, services up/uses below — e.g. **TCP/IP stack**.
**Model** (data + business logic), **View** (UI + input), **Controller** (mediates). User→View→Controller→Model→View. Separation of concerns; multiple views.

**Event-driven:** producers/consumers/channels — loose coupling (Node.js). **Blackboard:** knowledge sources + shared blackboard + control (expert systems). **Client-server:** requestors vs providers (2/3/n-tier).
Coincidental → Logical → Temporal → Procedural → Communicational → Sequential → **Functional (best)**. Aim for **functional cohesion**.
**Data (best)** → Stamp → Control → External → Common (shared globals) → **Content (worst)**. Aim for **data coupling**.

Goal: **high cohesion, low coupling** (decomposable, composable, localised change). A **trust boundary** separates components of different security levels — crossing it needs authn + authz + secure comms.
Small, **independently deployable** services, each with **its own database**, communicating only via **network APIs**, organised around business capabilities.

**Monolith:** one unit, shared DB, in-process. **SOA:** services over an **ESB**. **Microservices:** independent deployables, own DB, lightweight HTTP/REST/gRPC, fine-grained scaling, high fault isolation.
**Strangler Fig:** route through a facade, migrate piece by piece, coexist, then retire the monolith. **Anti-Corruption Layer:** translation layer to legacy systems (data/domain mapping).
Operational complexity · inter-service comms (retries, **circuit breakers**, fallbacks) · data consistency (**saga** pattern) · testing complexity · DevOps overhead · distributed security.
**Provided = lollipop (ball)**; **Required = socket (cup)**; an **assembly connector** joins ball→socket. Component = `<<component>>`, replaceable black-box via interfaces.
**Public port** drawn over the boundary (accessible); **private** drawn inside. **Usage dependency**: client needs supplier (dashed arrow `<<use>>`). Subsystem = logical grouping.
**Abstraction** = focus on essentials, ignore detail (a *level* concept). **Information hiding / encapsulation** = conceal internals behind an interface to cut coupling (an *access* concept).
**Lifelines** (object existence), **messages** (arrows), **activation boxes** (active processing), **return messages** (dashed), **alt fragments** (conditional). Shows interactions over **time**.
Concurrency (thread safety, deadlock), non-functional requirements, data persistence (DB/caching), event handling (observer/queues), error & exception handling.

**API** = source-level contract between components. **ABI** = binary-level contract with the OS/platform (data sizes, calling conventions, registers, file formats). **ABI breakage** breaks compiled binaries even with unchanged source.
**Sync** = caller blocks until done (e.g. `requests.get()`). **Async** = caller continues, results via callbacks/promises/events (e.g. Node.js) — scales for high concurrency.

**Fail-fast:** detect/report errors as early as possible (validate inputs/preconditions). **Graceful degradation:** keep partial functionality during failure (fallbacks, isolation). Good systems do both.
**Hawaiian missile alert (2018)** — no test/live distinction, no recovery, 38-min panic. **Therac-25** — cryptic 'Malfunction 54', override culture. Usability = safety, not cosmetics.
**L**earnability, **E**fficiency, **S**atisfaction, **E**rrors (prevention/recovery), **M**emorability (recognition over recall).
**Dogfooding** = the team uses its own product internally before release. **Wizard of Oz** = a human secretly simulates system responses while users test a mockup (great for AI/conversational UIs).

OpenSSL didn't validate the TLS heartbeat **length field** vs actual payload → **buffer over-read** leaking keys/tokens. A **QA-process** failure: no review, no fuzzing/boundary tests, no quality gates.
**Operation** (correctness, reliability, efficiency, integrity, usability), **Revision** (maintainability, testability, flexibility), **Transition** (portability, reusability, interoperability).

cards.front: Measure vs Metric + Cost of Quality
cards.back: **Measure** = raw count (defects); **Metric** = relationship (defects/KLOC). **COQ** = **COGQ** (prevention + appraisal) + **COPQ** (internal + external failure). Prevention is cheapest.
Systematic **monitoring of the development *process*** (not just final inspection), across the whole lifecycle: audits, deviation management, quality gates, defect management, traceability.

Expedient shortcuts that make future change costlier (hurts **maintainability/evolvability**). Quadrant: **Reckless/Prudent × Deliberate/Inadvertent** — acceptable kind = **Prudent + Deliberate**. ≠ plain defects.
Lost **$460M in 45 min**: deployed to **7 of 8 servers**, obsolete code live, manual deploy, no circuit breakers. Anti-patterns: no QA, bad version control, slow QA, manual-labour reliance.

**Red** (write a failing test) → **Green** (simplest code to pass) → **Refactor** (improve structure, same behaviour, tests stay green). Benefits: coverage, regression safety, living documentation, better design.
